title: Autogen agentchat: writing long documents - Any ideas?
body:
Hi all,

I really like the agentchat. Mainly because it works well with local models and it seems to produce quite good results (especially when comparing it to other agent solutions).

I wanted to ask you for crazy ideas: my goal is to come up with a setup able to write longer papers / documents on a specific topic. Of course, token size is always the limiting factor when using an LLM. You can't have your setup go over the token limit so whatever the final output is... it will be limited. No way to get a book out of one single prompt.

I wanted to explore some agentchat powered solutions that would allow a flexible output length and came to a few ideas:
1) Work with a "structurer" agent that writes a high level structure, another agent distributing the work over various "writers" who then focus on a part of the structure and "write" it. The downside may be that the maximum output length is merely the total token length x the number of writers.
2) Work with a "scribe" agent that has functions to append, summarise, read, write text files and interacts with a writer agent who constantly improves / appends, re-reads the output document.
3)...

Maybe some of you smarter than me have a good idea or even some experience on whether there is a winning approach? Otherwise I just play around with them but generally I would love some good or quirky ideas from the community.

title: Tutorial - Running Autogen using a local LLM running in oobabooga WebUI served via LiteLLM
body:
Suggesting you have Python, Autogen and oobabooga WebUI installed and running fine:

1. Install LiteLLM

``` 
pip install litellm 
```

2.  Install the openai API extension in the oobabooga WebUI

In the folder where the WebUI is installed:

``` cd extensions
cd openai
pip install -r requirements.txt 
```

Run the WebUI with the openai extension enabled:

``` 
python server.py --extensions openai 
```

3. Create a python file (f.e. test.py) with the following code:

``` from litellm import completion
import openai

openai.api_key ='sk-1111111111111111111111111111111' # no real api-key needed!

response = completion(
  model="oobabooga/TheBloke_WizardCoder-Python-13B-V1.0-GPTQ",
  messages=[{ "content": "Hi! How are you?","role": "user"}],
  api_base="http://127.0.0.1:5001/api",
  custom_llm_provider="openai",
  max_tokens=4000
)

print(response['choices'][0]['message']['content']) 
```

4. Run LiteLLM to serve the LLM-Model loaded in the WebUI:

``` 
litellm --model oobabooga/TheBloke_WizardCoder-Python-13B-V1.0-GPTQ
```

In this example the model TheBloke_WizardCoder-Python-13B-V1.0-GPTQ is used. 

5. Now run the python file

```
python test.py
```

You should get a useful response to the question "Hi! How are you?". 

6. If it works as intended the fun part begins. Create a new pyhton file (f.e. test-autogen.py) with the following code:

```
from autogen import AssistantAgent, UserProxyAgent, oai, GroupChat, GroupChatManager
config_list=[
    {
        "model": "oobabooga/TheBloke_WizardCoder-Python-13B-V1.0-GPTQ",
        "api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:5001/api",
        "api_type": "open_ai",
        "api_key": "NULL", # required, you don´t need to change this
        }
]


llm_config={
    "config_list": config_list,
}

coder = AssistantAgent(
    name="Coder",
    system_message="You write the code to solve the required Task. Implement improvements provided by the critic.",
    llm_config=llm_config,
)

critic = AssistantAgent(
    name="critic",
    system_message="You will make sure that the code provided by coder is bug free and all requirements are met. also provide coder with ideas for more features that make the project better. do not provide any code.",
    llm_config=llm_config
)

user_proxy = UserProxyAgent(
    name="user_proxy",
    system_message="A human admin wo will give the idea and run the code provided by Coder.",
    human_input_mode="ALWAYS",
    is_termination_msg=lambda x: x.get("content", "").rstrip().endswith("TERMINATE"),
)

groupchat = GroupChat(agents=[user_proxy, coder, critic], messages=[], max_round=12)
manager = GroupChatManager(groupchat=groupchat, llm_config=llm_config)
user_proxy.initiate_chat(manager, message="Write a calculator app using tkinter for the gui. the GUI Layout should resemble the layout of a casio calculator.", clear_history=False, config_list=config_list)

```

If everything works fine a groupchat should begin with the task to write code for a calculator app.

7. Possible problems:

I had multiple errors where the script ran into timeouts. If you have the same problem here is the fix that worked for me. I used the Pycharm IDE so the filepaths maybe different for you but the filenames are the same: 

Locate the file **api_requestor.py** (path on my system: venv/Lib/site-packages/openai/api_requestor.py) and change the "TIMEOUT_SECS = 600" to 6000.

In the file **completition.py** (path on my system: venv/Lib/site-packages/autogen/oai/completion.py) change the "request_timeout = 60" to 600.

8. Have fun!!

I made some modifications to your code sample, replacing it with my own model instead of GPT-4. Initially, everything went smoothly. However, when I used the following code, the Langchain_AutoGen() function couldn't access and read local files. On the other hand, the agentchat_groupchat() function worked perfectly, delivering the same quality as GPT-4.
I didn't use Docker; instead, I installed the package directly in a Conda environment using pip.
```
import autogen
from accelerate import Accelerator
accelerator = Accelerator()
config_list_baichuan2=[
    {
        "model": "Baichuan2-13b-base",
        "api_base": "http://localhost:8000/v1",
        "api_type": "open_ai",
        "api_key": "NULL",
    }
]

def agentchat_groupchat():
    # 定义LLM配置
    llm_config = {
        "seed": 42,  # 更改种子以进行不同的尝试
        "temperature": 0,
        "config_list": config_list_baichuan2,
        "request_timeout": 120,
    }

    # 创建用户代理
    user_proxy = autogen.UserProxyAgent(
        name="User_proxy",
        system_message="人类管理员。",
        code_execution_config={"last_n_messages": 2, "work_dir": "groupchat"},
        human_input_mode="TERMINATE"
    )

    # 创建编码代理
    coder = autogen.AssistantAgent(
        name="Coder",
        llm_config=llm_config,
    )

    # 创建产品经理代理
    pm = autogen.AssistantAgent(
        name="Product_manager",
        system_message="在软件产品创意中具有创造性。",
        llm_config=llm_config,
    )

    # 定义群聊
    groupchat = autogen.GroupChat(agents=[user_proxy, coder, pm], messages=[], max_round=12)
    
    # 创建群聊管理器
    manager = autogen.GroupChatManager(groupchat=groupchat, llm_config=llm_config)

    # 用户代理启动与管理器的聊天，寻找关于arxiv上的gpt-4的最新论文，并找到其在软件中的潜在应用
    user_proxy.initiate_chat(manager, message="在arxiv上找到关于gpt-4的最新论文，并找到其在软件中的潜在应用。")
    
    # 输入exit来终止聊天


def Langchain_AutoGen():
    # 通用导入
    from langchain.pydantic_v1 import BaseModel, Field
    from langchain.tools import BaseTool
    from typing import Optional, Type
    import math

    # 定义计算圆周长的工具的输入模型
    class CircumferenceToolInput(BaseModel):
        radius: float = Field()

    # 定义计算圆周长的工具
    class CircumferenceTool(BaseTool):
        name = "circumference_calculator"
        description = "当你需要使用圆的半径计算圆周长时使用此工具"
        args_schema: Type[BaseModel] = CircumferenceToolInput

        # 定义如何计算圆周长
        def _run(self, radius: float):
            return float(radius) * 2.0 * math.pi

    # 导入文件读取工具
    from langchain.tools.file_management.read import ReadFileTool

    # 定义一个从LangChain工具生成llm_config的函数
    def generate_llm_config(tool):
        # 基于工具的args_schema定义函数模式
        function_schema = {
            "name": tool.name.lower().replace(' ', '_'),
            "description": tool.description,
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {},
                "required": [],
            },
        }

        if tool.args is not None:
            function_schema["parameters"]["properties"] = tool.args

        return function_schema

    # 实例化读取文件的工具
    read_file_tool = ReadFileTool()
    custom_tool = CircumferenceTool()

    # 构造llm_config
    llm_config = {
        # 为工具生成函数配置
        "functions": [
            generate_llm_config(custom_tool),
            generate_llm_config(read_file_tool),
        ],
        "config_list": config_list_baichuan2,  # 假设你在其他地方已经定义了这个
        "request_timeout": 120,
    }

    print(llm_config)

    # 创建用户代理
    user_proxy = autogen.UserProxyAgent(
        name="user_proxy",
        is_termination_msg=lambda x: x.get("content", "") and x.get("content", "").rstrip().endswith("TERMINATE"),
        human_input_mode="NEVER",
        max_consecutive_auto_reply=10,
        code_execution_config={"work_dir": "coding"},
    )

    # 在用户代理中注册工具并开始对话
    user_proxy.register_function(
        function_map={
            custom_tool.name: custom_tool._run,
            read_file_tool.name: read_file_tool._run,
        }
    )

    # 创建助手代理
    chatbot = autogen.AssistantAgent(
        name="chatbot",
        system_message="对于编码任务，只使用你所提供的函数。当任务完成时回复TERMINATE。",
        llm_config=llm_config,
    )

    # 初始化与助手代理的对话
    user_proxy.initiate_chat(
        chatbot,
        message="读取文件路径为'Test.txt'的文件，然后计算文件内容作为半径的圆的周长。",  # 文件中为"7.81mm"
        llm_config=llm_config,
    )

if __name__ == '__main__':
    Langchain_AutoGen()
```

title: Teachability vs codebase
body:
Off-the-cuff, teachability sounds like a game changer for code-assisting LMs, but what are the limitations? We have a proprietary codebase with hundreds of 1st-party C++ cmake-library targets, and hundreds more 3rd party libraries.

In theory it seems like I could set up a multi-group autogen with the goal of studying the codebase and being able to detect replicated functionalities, redundant implementations, detached spaghetti code, and answer "how do I?" questions.

But is that stretching the practical limitations of memory? Is this an undertaking that would be better achieved by extending training of a model like Llama2 or something with the codebase?

title: Subclassing the vector dB to instead use a PostgreSQL dB for retrieval agents.
body:
Hi, I just wanted to share a subclass I was working on and I know others probably would like to use it as well. Please let me know if you see any issues and if you found this helpful. This does not handle the structure of your db and does not embed new documents or text. I'm sorry for the formatting of the post, this is my first one.


```python
Base = declarative_base()


class lt_storage(Base):

    __tablename__ = 'lt_storage'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    text = Column(String)  
    code = Column(Text)  
    embedding = Column(Vector(1536))



class SQLRetrieveUserProxyAgent(RetrieveUserProxyAgent):

    def __init__(self, db_url, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.engine = create_engine(db_url)
        self.Session = sessionmaker(bind=self.engine)


    def query_vector_db(
            self,
            query_texts: List[str],
            n_results: int = 10,
            search_string: str = "",
            **kwargs,
    ) -> Dict[str, Union[List[List[int]], List[List[str]]]]:
        master_doc_ids = []
        master_doc_texts = []

        session = self.Session()
        for query in query_texts:

            query_vector = embeddings.embed_query(query)

            results = session.execute(
                select(lt_storage.id, lt_storage.text)
                .where(
                    lt_storage.text.contains(search_string),
                )
                .order_by(lt_storage.embedding.cosine_distance(query_vector))
                .limit(n_results)
            ).fetchall()

            doc_ids = [result.id for result in results]
            doc_texts = [result.text for result in results]

            master_doc_ids.append(doc_ids)
            master_doc_texts.append(doc_texts)

        session.close()

        return {"ids": master_doc_ids, "documents": master_doc_texts}

    def retrieve_docs(self, problem: str, n_results: int = 20, search_string: str = "", **kwargs):
        results = self.query_vector_db(
            query_texts=[problem],
            n_results=n_results,
            search_string=search_string,
            **kwargs,
        )

        self._results = results
        print("doc_ids: ", results["ids"])

```

title: Examples of how to register a reply function
body:
@xmi1an you can hook in function that is called whenever an agent receives a message. 

Assuming you have two agents `user_proxy` and `assistant`, you can [register a function](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/docs/reference/agentchat/conversable_agent#conversableagent-objects) with these agents that gets called with some parameters. 

```python

def print_messages(recipient, messages, sender, config): 
    if "callback" in config and  config["callback"] is not None:
        callback = config["callback"]
        callback(sender, recipient, messages[-1])
    print(f"Messages sent to: {recipient.name} | num messages: {len(messages)}")
    return False, None  # required to ensure the agent communication flow continues

user_proxy.register_reply(
    [autogen.Agent, None],
    reply_func=print_messages, 
    config={"callback": None},
)

assistant.register_reply(
    [autogen.Agent, None],
    reply_func=print_messages, 
    config={"callback": None},
) 
``` 

In the above, we register a `print_messages` message that is called each time the agent receive a message.

_Originally posted by @victordibia in https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues/478#issuecomment-1785922097_

It's a good example to add to FAQ.

title: Devil's Advocate Pattern
body:
One of the benefits of pair programming are those moments when they say "I'm going to call that function, <pause>, because I'm not worrying about performance" and you say "but this IS the core of the hot path, this method will happen inside the core loop for every iteration".

I see a lot of tokens wasted because a bad suggestion introduces a token and if its in an attention spot, some models will never let up (ask codellama to "implement std::forward. do not include utility. do not use remove_reference", and it will either say "this is my implementation not using remove_reference: .. forward ... remove_reference ... or it will give you one of the s/o alternatives to this question but with 'remove_pointer'.

What I want is a fan-out pattern: Agent A -> {Agent B + Agent C ...} (in parallel or serial) with a reduce return path. That is, Agent A will basically predict which response is better and return that.

Use cases: comparing alternatives from different models or different seeds or different specialists ("you care about perf, you care about idiomatic correctness") or different providers (gcp vs azure). Especially with access to memory this will be super useful for LMs with memory of a LARGE code base.

title: How should I structure data for fine-tuning a model in a groupchat setting?
body:
I'm trying to finetune some llm agents such that they perform some specialized task. However, I am unsure of how to best convert an Autogen groupchat conversation into a training format.

For example, let's say I'm working with the following conversation:
```
User prompt
Agent 1 speaks
Agent 2 speaks
Agent 3 speaks
```
Now let's say I'm trying to fine-tune Agent 3 here, which is backed by a Llama 2 model

Llama 2 model format:
```
<s>[INST] <<SYS>>
{{ system_prompt }}
<</SYS>>

{{ user_msg_1 }} [/INST] {{ model_answer_1 }} </s><s>[INST] {{ user_msg_2 }} [/INST]
```

How should I go about structuring this into training data? The 3 ways I've thought about are:

### Option 1: Treat other Agent responses as separate user responses
```
<s>[INST] <<SYS>>
{{ system_prompt }}
<</SYS>>

{{ User prompt }} [/INST] {{ Agent 1 output }} [/INST] {{ Agent 2 output }} [/INST] </s><s>[INST] {{ Agent 3 output }} [/INST]
```

### Option 2: Combine other Agent responses into single User response
```
<s>[INST] <<SYS>>
{{ system_prompt }}
<</SYS>>

{{ User prompt }} {{ Agent 1 output }} {{ Agent 2 output }} [/INST] </s><s>[INST] {{ Agent 3 output }} [/INST]
```

### Option 3: Treat other Agent responses as AI responses
```
<s>[INST] <<SYS>>
{{ system_prompt }}
<</SYS>>

{{ User prompt }} [/INST] </s><s>[INST] {{ Agent 1 output }} [/INST] [INST] {{ Agent 2 output }} [/INST] [INST] {{ Agent 3 output }} [/INST]
```

Do any of these look viable? Or should I try and roll my own new format which would be more compatible with groupchat conversations?

title: Method towards AGI with MemGPT and AutoGen
body:
### **Method towards AGI with MemGPT and AutoGen**

_Note: The following is just some quick examples of the reletively rapid improvments that could be made to the MemGPT/AutoGen hybrid software solution that would enable dramatic improvements to requests to complete goals, tasks, or problems. Function calls would need to be aligned to “ChatGPT Response 2”, which could be streamlined and expanded upon._

**Question 1:**

If an LLM is instructed to read, write, understand, and update a text document every time the LLM interacts with a user, what English text could be stored within the text document that would provide logic and reasoning skills to the LLM that would also allow it to expand upon that logic and reasoning skills?

**ChatGPT Response 1:**

The concept of having a large language model (LLM) like GPT-4 read, write, understand, and update a text document in each interaction to improve its logic and reasoning skills is an interesting one. While LLMs don't "learn" in the traditional sense from each interaction (as their learning happens during the training phase on a fixed dataset), there are certain types of texts that can be useful in this scenario. Here are some suggestions:
1.	Philosophical Texts: Works that cover logic, ethics, epistemology, and other branches of philosophy. These texts often involve complex reasoning and argumentation, which can serve as good examples for developing reasoning skills.
2.	Scientific Literature: Papers and articles from fields like physics, biology, and computer science. These documents often include logical structures, hypothesis testing, and evidence-based reasoning.
3.	Mathematical and Logical Puzzles: Problems and puzzles that require logical reasoning and problem-solving skills. These can include classic logic puzzles, mathematical problems, and other brainteasers.
4.	Critical Thinking and Argumentation Texts: Books or articles that teach critical thinking skills, argumentation techniques, and logical fallacies. These texts can help the model understand how to construct and deconstruct arguments effectively.
5.	Historical Texts and Case Studies: Detailed analyses of historical events or case studies from various fields. These texts often involve understanding complex situations, drawing inferences from limited information, and making connections between different events.
6.	Literary Analysis: Works of literary criticism and analysis, which require understanding themes, motives, and symbolic representations in various forms of literature.
7.	Legal Documents and Case Law: Legal texts, including laws, legal cases, and judgments, which involve complex reasoning and interpretation of legal language and principles.
8.	Interactive and Recursive Texts: Texts designed specifically for the purpose of teaching reasoning, such as interactive fiction or texts that encourage the reader to make predictions and then provide feedback.
9.	AI and Machine Learning Research Papers: To understand the limits and capabilities of AI, including discussions on AI ethics, safety, and potential.
10.	Cross-Disciplinary Research: Texts that integrate knowledge from multiple fields, encouraging holistic thinking and the ability to connect disparate concepts.
However, it's important to note that while exposing an LLM to such texts might provide a rich context for its responses, the LLM doesn't inherently "expand" its logic and reasoning skills like a human learner would. Its abilities are constrained by its training and the algorithms that govern its function. The LLM can simulate understanding and reasoning based on patterns it has learned, but it doesn't develop these skills autonomously.

**Question 2:**

Please thoroughly understand the following and work through your answer step by step. A human student can read and follow instructions or processes previously written by a human teacher, which enable the human student to solve previously unseen problems by the human student. These instructions are reusable in different situations and can be combined with additional instructions or processes from the human teacher, enabling the human student to continue to develop unique processes to solve new goals, problems, or tasks once the goal or problem is understood. This previous situation should be able to be replicated for artificial intelligence. If a large language model (LLM) is combined with MemGPT (enabling a long-term memory database and ability to do function calls to that memory) in combination with AutoGen (enabling multiple agents to work together which replicates a human having internal dialog and thought processes) then if the long-term memory database contains a set of general methods for hypothesis testing, evidence-based reasoning, logical reasoning, problem-solving skills, drawing inferences from limited information, making connections between different processes, etc., then each time a user provides a new goal, problem, or task the LLM can search through the long-term memory database for the best matching combination of hypothesis testing, evidence-based reasoning, logical reasoning, problem-solving skills, etc. processes in order to provide the user with the best solution to the goal, problem, or task. What specific text based English instructions can be written to store within the LLM’s long-term memory database that the LLM can follow to provide a framework for hypothesis testing, evidence-based reasoning, logical reasoning, problem-solving skills, drawing inferences from limited information, making connections between different processes, etc.? These textual instructions/processes should be written as short and concise instructions/processes with accurate label identifiers, which will enable the LLM to quickly use function calls to locate the correct combination of instructions/processes needed to best complete the requested goal, problem, or task. Keep in mind that these instructions/processes must be able to be applied to a broad range of situations. 

**ChatGPT Response 2:**

The idea of replicating human-like learning and problem-solving in a large language model (LLM) involves creating a framework where the model can access and apply a set of general methods for reasoning and problem-solving. The integration of technologies like MemGPT and AutoGen can potentially facilitate this by providing long-term memory and multi-agent collaboration, respectively. Here’s a step-by-step approach to creating a set of textual instructions or processes for this purpose:

**1. Hypothesis Testing**
Label: _HypothesisTestingProcedure_
Instructions:
•	Identify the problem or question.
•	Formulate a hypothesis that offers a potential solution or explanation.
•	Determine the variables and plan an approach to test the hypothesis.
•	Collect and analyze data relevant to the hypothesis.
•	Interpret the results to either support or refute the hypothesis.
•	Conclude based on the evidence and consider alternative explanations.

**2. Evidence-Based Reasoning**
Label: _EvidenceBasedReasoningMethod_
Instructions:
•	Define the issue or claim to be evaluated.
•	Gather all relevant evidence, ensuring a range of perspectives.
•	Critically assess the quality and reliability of the evidence.
•	Analyze the evidence in relation to the issue or claim.
•	Draw conclusions based on the balance and weight of the evidence.
•	Reflect on the strength of the conclusions and identify any biases or gaps.

**3. Logical Reasoning**
Label: _LogicalReasoningFramework_
Instructions:
•	Clearly state the premises or assumptions.
•	Use logical operations (e.g., deduction, induction) to derive conclusions.
•	Check for logical consistency and coherence in the argument.
•	Identify any logical fallacies or errors in reasoning.
•	Test the argument against different scenarios or counterexamples.
•	Finalize the reasoning process with a logically sound conclusion.

**4. Problem-Solving Skills**
Label: _ProblemSolvingGuideline_
Instructions:
•	Define and understand the problem.
•	Break the problem down into smaller, manageable parts.
•	Generate potential solutions or strategies.
•	Evaluate each solution's feasibility and impact.
•	Select the most effective solution and plan its implementation.
•	Execute the plan and monitor its effectiveness, adjusting as necessary.

**5. Inference from Limited Information**
Label: _InferenceDrawingTechnique_
Instructions:
•	Identify the information available.
•	Recognize the gaps in information.
•	Use relevant knowledge and principles to infer missing details.
•	Consider multiple possibilities and scenarios.
•	Evaluate the likelihood of each inference.
•	Choose the most probable inferences while remaining open to new information.

**6. Making Connections Between Processes**
Label: _ProcessConnectionStrategy_
Instructions:
•	List the processes or concepts involved.
•	Identify common elements or patterns between them.
•	Explore potential interactions and relationships.
•	Synthesize a unified understanding or framework.
•	Apply this integrative perspective to the task at hand.
•	Continuously update as new connections or insights emerge.

**Implementation in an LLM Context**
•	Storage: Store these instructions in the LLM's long-term memory (facilitated by MemGPT).
•	Function Calls: Enable function calls to these instructions based on the task or query at hand.
•	Combination and Application: Use AutoGen's multi-agent system to dynamically combine different instructions based on the specific problem or goal.
•	Adaptation: Allow the LLM to adapt these processes to the context of the problem, drawing on its vast knowledge base and the specific data of the situation.

**Considerations**
•	Flexibility: These instructions should be applied flexibly, adapting to the context and specifics of each task.
•	Continuous Learning: While this approach provides a structured framework, it's crucial to remember that current LLMs do not learn or evolve their understanding autonomously post-training.
•	Ethical and Practical Limitations: The quality of output will depend on the LLM's training and inherent limitations. Ethical considerations, such as bias and misuse, must be managed carefully.

This framework attempts to mimic some aspects of human problem-solving and learning within the constraints of current AI capabilities. While it can enhance the LLM's performance in specific tasks, it's important to recognize the differences between this simulated problem-solving and genuine human cognitive processes.

title: ConversableAgent class needs much love
body:
What do we think about [conversable_agent.py](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/main/autogen/agentchat/conversable_agent.py) ?

It feels like it's well on its way to becoming a tangled web of tears. There are so many patterns happening. I've been wanting to refactor it but don't want to bother unless maintainers see the Matrix with me.. I feel like we could do without a lot of what's going on here and implement:

- some nice chainable observers.
- separation of some of these concerns
- single responsibility principal
- use pydantic for most the things
- replace these one-line class property methods
- deduplicate all the async
- no more what seems like factory, command, and strategy patterns altogether
- maybe more composition. Maybe not though. Probably leave most of the subclassing alone until last or later.

To be clear, I'm not hating on the code. Technical debt is what we do. I did something similar myself recently with a command factory that used dependency injection, and though it technically worked, I had to get rid of it because it was just too cool.

I'm happy to be wrong if I am.

title: Autogen Studio: LLM model defined per agent - makes it VERY hard to switch to test models! Need duplicate agents for every model??
body:
Installed Autogen Studio today
Seems really cool. But a big downside I've already noticed, is that if we want to do a research task on GPT4, then also try Mixtral, or whatever, we have to either
a) go edit the agents, and delete the model GPT4, add in the model for something else
or
b) duplicate the agents so we have a research assistant that is basically identical in all aspects except the model they use.

Am I the only one that thinks this is clunky?
There has to be a better way.

If I want to run a group of say, 3-5 agents, that 10 agents to try 2 models. 15 agents to try 3 models. etc.
UI is gonna get messy real quick.

Now say I want to edit that agent. But I have 2-3 or more of them, that are identical again except for the agent specified.
(or I'm editing the LLM priority order every time I want to use a different model).

I've had this running less than 30mins and I've already hit this clunkiness of multiple agents that do the same thing, or spending tedious minutes each time re-configuring what LLM each agent should use.

Hoping others may have an insight into a better way the LLMs could be defined?

My solution? Not sure...
But maybe this is why other tools use a flowchart style workflow to build agents, because then you can easily see the order of operations AND quickly specify whatever you need per node. 
If I could see the workflow as an actual **_flow_** of nodes, they could have dropdowns. Say one overall dropdown or node where you could quickly specify default LLM for any nodes in which the LLM was not explicitly defined, and a dropdown IN the nodes if you wanted an override one, such that an agent used a different LLM to the default for the flow.

Current implementation is way too many boxes, modals, windows in which I need to go edit LLM!

Why isn't the function not available?

title: Implementing Autonomous Agent Generation and Integration in AutoGen Studio using Extended AutoBuild Capabilities
body:
Description:

The current functionality of AutoGen Studio, a platform for creating and managing digital agents in multi-agent workflows, involves significant manual input for the configuration and integration of new agents. While the AutoBuild pipeline introduced by AutoGen automates the building of multi-agent systems for complex tasks, it still requires initial user-provided descriptions and configurations. This proposal suggests extending the capabilities of AutoBuild into AutoGen Studio to enable autonomous agent generation and integration.
Objective:

The aim is to enhance AutoGen Studio by allowing existing agents to autonomously generate and integrate new agents into workflows, based on dynamically assessed requirements. This feature would reduce manual intervention, improve response times to changing workflow demands, and increase overall system scalability and flexibility.
Proposed Features:

    Dynamic Agent Creation: Enable agents within AutoGen Studio to autonomously create new agents when specific criteria or triggers are met within a workflow.
    Intelligent Agent Integration: Newly created agents should be capable of seamlessly integrating into existing workflows, understanding their role, and beginning their tasks without manual setup.
    Adaptive Workflow Management: Agents should assess workflow demands in real-time and decide when new agents are needed, what skills they should possess, and how they should be configured.
    Security and Compliance Checks: Include mechanisms to ensure that the autonomous creation and integration of agents adhere to security standards and industry-specific compliance requirements.
    Performance Monitoring and Reporting: Implement monitoring tools to track the performance of autonomously created agents, providing feedback for further optimization.
    User Oversight and Control: Despite the autonomy, users should have the final say in the creation and integration of agents, with options to manually override or adjust the automated processes.

Use Cases:

    Scalable Customer Support: In a customer support scenario, as the number of queries increases, the system could autonomously generate specialized agents to handle specific query types, improving response times and efficiency.
    Dynamic Resource Allocation in Project Management: In project management, new agents could be created to manage unexpected tasks or changes in project scope, ensuring adaptive resource allocation.
    Real-time Data Analysis and Reporting: For data-intensive industries, agents could be generated to handle sudden influxes of data, ensuring timely analysis and reporting.

Potential Challenges:

    Security Risks: Autonomous agent creation could pose security risks, necessitating robust security protocols.
    Quality Control: Ensuring that autonomously created agents maintain a high standard of performance and relevance to the task.
    Resource Management: Balancing the computational resources used by newly created agents to avoid inefficiencies.

Conclusion:

Extending the AutoBuild capabilities into AutoGen Studio to facilitate autonomous agent generation and integration would significantly enhance the platform's utility and efficiency. This feature aligns with the growing need for dynamic and scalable multi-agent systems in various industries.

title: Agent Session Based Workflow & Management Concept
body:
_Regarding Autogen & Autogen Studio_
tldr; add functionality to autogen to execute workflows across individual agent sessions to leverage memory and context to improve output quality.    

**Problem:**  LLM / API Text gen quality substantial increases over the course of individual sessions due to user feedback and context.  Some models are heavy on pleasantries/ monologues / unnecessary disclaimers and wordy explanations which rapidly go away over the course of an individual session, likely due to substantial context/memory taking over that space (maybe that's why some top tier pre-prompts are super long).  

**Autogen workflows can struggle to achieve that quality due to limitations of memory/context across workflows.**  

**Solution Concept:** Agent Sessions would be a new feature for autogen which would enable the creation and assignment of individual chat sessions to a workflow.  A workflow would essentially be executing across individual agent sessions in real time. 

![ui_concept_AGStudio-02](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/assets/141588235/ec6967b7-4f2f-43d0-9f4f-909354342379)
![ui_concept_AGStudio-03](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/assets/141588235/47f53d86-e209-45c1-9060-e61a18960233)
_(i do not recommend these models or this workflow its all improvised to convey the concept of the same agent being optimized for tasks via sessions)_

When configuring a workflow, the user would assign an agent as well as an individual agent session to the workflow, interactions with that agent happen within that session instance and the context/memory of that individual session is included along with the workflow context.  

After a workflow is completed, a user can navigate to any agent's individual session instance and has the options to tweak parameters and even message the agent in its own chat's log context (outside of a workflow).   This is the view my mockup concept was portraying. 

![ui_concept_AGStudio-01](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/assets/141588235/938b5ef9-03d4-49fc-b5b1-195b76400374)

Options in this screen include the ability to edit, regenerate, or delete responses for the sake of improved context and testing.  Edits to the session do not roll up into the workflows own session/log.  Also the ability to assign/change Model at the session level is here as well.    

This can also be a way to **provide feedback to an agent**.  LLM memory context can degrade over time, so an option added to the mockup of additional pre-prompt insert can be a way to capture important information used for pre-prompting/memory.  Also a slider is available to adjust how much of the individual sessions memory/context is included when executing a workflow.

In the playground in Autogen studio an option also would be available to create a new individual 1 on 1 session with an agent.  this allows for testing of the agent's configuration as well as an ability to **temper an agent before it's assigned a workflow**.  

The end result would be providing the end user powerful tools to experiment with and improve their desired result with any individual agent, gaining substantially more milage out of models that other wise would need more tuning.  

The mockup below is only to demonstrate some functionality from a UI standpoint, workflow setting pictured on the left obviously wouldn't be located there but is demonstrating a dropdown to select a session when creating a workflow.  

**Interaction with an agent at session level can help with:**
- Carrying relevant context into future workflows
- Priming/Testing Agents before Workflow execution
- Expediting prompt optimization
- Troubleshooting undesired results 
- Regenerating a specific step of a workflow without having to re-run the entire workflow
- Model Testing/Swapping in an existing context

Just some ideas.

title: Visual enhancement to `visualize_speaker_transitions_dict`
body:
Getting to know the [visualization tool](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8ec1c3e0b3aeb130eab21e682f2c4fe393706eb6/autogen/graph_utils.py#L113) for speakers, my first try resulted in text being cut-off and arrows occasionally being hidden by text labels 
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/assets/15487280/8cfe1571-94e9-4c26-a3d4-c08770c11150)

I made some updates seen below to fix those issue:
```
def visualize_speaker_transitions_dict(speaker_transitions_dict: dict, agents: List[Agent]):
    """
    Visualize the speaker_transitions_dict using networkx, with increased figure size and adjusted layout.
    """
    try:
        import networkx as nx
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    except ImportError as e:
        logging.fatal("Failed to import networkx or matplotlib. Try running 'pip install autogen[graphs]'")
        raise e

    G = nx.DiGraph()

    # Add nodes
    G.add_nodes_from([agent.name for agent in agents])

    # Add edges
    for key, value in speaker_transitions_dict.items():
        for agent in value:
            G.add_edge(key.name, agent.name)

    # Set the figure size
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

    # Visualize
    pos = nx.spring_layout(G)  # For consistent positioning

    # Draw nodes and edges
    nx.draw_networkx_nodes(G, pos)
    nx.draw_networkx_edges(G, pos)

    # Draw labels below the nodes
    label_pos = {k: [v[0], v[1] - 0.1] for k, v in pos.items()}  # Shift labels below the nodes
    nx.draw_networkx_labels(G, label_pos, verticalalignment='top', font_color="darkgreen")

    # Adding margins
    ax = plt.gca()
    ax.margins(0.1)  # Increase the margin value if needed


    # Adding a dynamic title
    total_transitions = sum(len(v) for v in speaker_transitions_dict.values())
    title = f'Agent Interactions: {len(agents)} Agents, {total_transitions} Potential Transitions'
    plt.title(title)

    plt.show()
```
![image](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/assets/15487280/289e9b69-84f5-4bba-8e29-27c8d9b7e8b6)

author: Nathan-Intergral

title: _summarize_chat can return a non-string object
body:
The _summarize_chat method is defined as so:
```python
    def _summarize_chat(
        self,
        summary_method,
        summary_args,
        recipient: Optional[Agent] = None,
        cache: Optional[AbstractCache] = None,
    ) -> str:
...
        if isinstance(summary_method, Callable):
            summary = summary_method(self, recipient, summary_args)
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                "If not None, the summary_method must be a string from [`reflection_with_llm`, `last_msg`] or a callable."
            )
        return summary
```

Seems that it is expected for registered replies to return a non-string result (this is a snippet from the register_reply docstrings):

```python
def reply_func(
    recipient: ConversableAgent,
    messages: Optional[List[Dict]] = None,
    sender: Optional[Agent] = None,
    config: Optional[Any] = None,
) -> Tuple[bool, Union[str, Dict, None]]:
```
Moreover, ChatResult seems to expect summary to be a string:
```python
@dataclass
class ChatResult:
    """(Experimental) The result of a chat. Almost certain to be changed."""

    chat_id: int = None
    """chat id"""
    chat_history: List[Dict[str, any]] = None
    """The chat history."""
    summary: str = None
    """A summary obtained from the chat."""
    cost: Dict[str, dict] = None  # keys: "usage_including_cached_inference", "usage_excluding_cached_inference"
    """The cost of the chat.
       The value for each usage type is a dictionary containing cost information for that specific type.
           - "usage_including_cached_inference": Cost information on the total usage, including the tokens in cached inference.
           - "usage_excluding_cached_inference": Cost information on the usage of tokens, excluding the tokens in cache. No larger than "usage_including_cached_inference".
    """
    human_input: List[str] = None
    """A list of human input solicited during the chat."""
```
To clarify, right now this means _summarize_chat returns a tuple when using a registered reply callable, which is clearly not the expected behavior. 

Its a minor thing, but I think it would be a good idea to:
- Check if the summary_method is returning a tuple, and return the second argument if so
- Update the summary return typings to be Union[str, any], or at least Union[str, Dict, None]

Hi, Guys!

Need help to solve a Problem.

I am trying to integrate autogen with a Chat API - But I'm blocked with some kind of logic block... Here's the problem:

I want to make the conversable agent ask for specific questions to, in the end, send a JSON to a route in my backend.
So, for it I made this prompt:

```
prompt = """
    'Receive a JSON with information about a proposer and ask the client the following questions, one at a time, in the listed order. Each question must be validated according to the provided instructions. If the answer is not valid, ask again until a valid answer is received.

    1. **Type of Proposer:**
    - Question: "What is the type of proposer? It should be 'F' for an individual or 'J' for a legal entity."
    - Validation: The answer must be 'F' or 'J'.

    2. **Document:**
    - Question: "What is the proposer's document number? It should be in the format of CPF (xxx.xxx.xxx-xx) for individuals or CNPJ (xx.xxx.xxx/xxxx-xx) for legal entities."
    - Validation: The answer must follow the CPF or CNPJ format depending on the type of proposer.

    3. **Email:**
    - Question: "What is the proposer's email?"
    - Validation: The answer must be a valid email address.

    4. **Name:**
    - Question: "What is the proposer's full name?"
    - Validation: The answer must be a valid full name.

Ensure to ask the questions in the correct order and validate each answer as described. If the answer is not valid, ask again until you get an answer that meets the specified requirements.
    
    Finally, provide me with a JSON of the information as per the example below:

    "proponent": {
            "type": "F",
            "document": "123.456.789-10",
            "email": "teste@teste.com.br",
            "name": "Roberto Braga",
        },
    """
```

**My goal is to receive a message through a POST route and deliver the response to that message. My actual objective is to make the Conversable Agent return the questions from my prompt until all are answered and then make a POST request to route X. Since each message is a request, it occasionally forgets and starts over in the middle of the conversation. How can I fix this?**


My code:
```

from autogen.agentchat.user_proxy_agent import UserProxyAgent
from autogen.agentchat.conversable_agent import ConversableAgent
from autogen.agentchat.contrib.capabilities.teachability import Teachability
import os


def get_quotation_message(message, contact):
    
    quote_chat = ConversableAgent('quote_chat', human_input_mode='NEVER',
                            llm_config={
                                "config_list": [
                                    {"model": "gpt-4o",
                                     "api_key": os.environ.get('OPENAI_API_KEY')}
                                ]},
                                system_message=prompt
                            )

    teachability = Teachability(
        reset_db=False,
        path_to_db_dir=f'./quote_dbs/{contact}'
    )

    teachability.add_to_agent(quote_chat)

    teachability.train_agent(quote_chat)


    user_proxy = UserProxyAgent(name="user_proxy")

    quote_chat.send(
        messages=message,
        recipient=quote_chat,
        request_reply=True
        )
    

    return quote_chat.get_last_message().text    
```


Can anyone help with it?

title: Discussion about nested_chats design
body:
The document describes that nested chat is a powerful conversation pattern that allows you to package complex workflows into a single agent.

I'm a bit confused about the nested chat design. The nested chat is implemented by registering the reply_func_from_nested_chats method. In this method, only the last_msg is used to initialize a new chat, causing the loss of other chat history. I feel that this is not consistent with the design of the generate_reply method, which accepts a message list.

```python
def _summary_from_nested_chats(
        chat_queue: List[Dict[str, Any]], recipient: Agent, messages: Union[str, Callable], sender: Agent, config: Any
    ) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        last_msg = messages[-1].get("content")
        chat_to_run = []
        for i, c in enumerate(chat_queue):
            current_c = c.copy()
            if current_c.get("sender") is None:
                current_c["sender"] = recipient
            message = current_c.get("message")
            # If message is not provided in chat_queue, we by default use the last message from the original chat history as the first message in this nested chat (for the first chat in the chat queue).
            # NOTE: This setting is prone to change.
            if message is None and i == 0:
                message = last_msg
            if callable(message):
                message = message(recipient, messages, sender, config)
            # We only run chat that has a valid message. NOTE: This is prone to change dependin on applications.
            if message:
                current_c["message"] = message
                chat_to_run.append(current_c)
        if not chat_to_run:
            return True, None
        res = initiate_chats(chat_to_run)
        return True, res[-1].summary
```

If I want to inject some context before the conversation, it won't work.

        "config_list": [{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "api_key": os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]}]}

        {"role": "system","content": "my name is agent"},
        {"role": "user","content": "what's your name?"},
    ])

```

body:
Hi,

I am new to autogen and I am trying out a new use case, with the help of multiple function tools. But now I am in confusion about how to achieve this. I have a function tool called kafka_consumer, which will keep listening to the server for new values. So my user_proxy agent will register this tool, I also have another tool called alert_tool that will also be registered, so in the Kafka consumer tool when an even number is received it should be able to send this back to the user proxy agent so that the user proxy agent can make another trigger call to send an alert using the send_alert tool. This should not close the initial Kafka consumer tool. so is there a way the tool can communicate back to the Agent and the agent can route the output from the tool to another function? the catch is that it should not exit my Kafka consumer tool, and an alert should be sent whenever the number is even.  The provided is my code snippet, and this is too dependent on a single function tool:

```
def send_alert(api: str, number: int):
    """Api to send alert
    """
    url = f"{api}?number={number}"

    try:
        # Perform the GET request to the API
        response = requests.get(url)

        # Check if the request was successful
        if response.status_code == 200:
            print(f"API Response: {response.text}")
        else:
            print(
                f"Failed to call API. Status code: {response.status_code}, Message: {response.text}"
            )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred: {e}")


@user_proxy.register_for_execution()
@coder.register_for_llm(description="Create a Kafka consumer for listening to a topic")
def KafkaConsumerTool(
    bootstrap_servers: Annotated[str, "Kafka bootstrap server for listening data from"],
    topic: Annotated[str, "Topic used in the kafka consumer for listening."],
    api: Annotated[str, "Api endpoint for sending alert"]
) -> str:
    """Kafka consumer tool
    """
    # Set up the Kafka consumer
    consumer = KafkaConsumer(
        topic,
        bootstrap_servers=bootstrap_servers,
        auto_offset_reset="earliest",
        group_id="even-number-consumers",
    )

    # Consume messages
    for message in consumer:
        number = int(message.value.decode("utf-8"))
        if number % 2 == 0:
            send_alert(api=api, number=number)


with Cache.disk() as cache:
    user_proxy.initiate_chat(
        coder,
        message="create a Kafka consumer and listen to the Kafka server that is \
            running on`localhost:9092` and topic `number` and print the result \
            send an alert to the api `http://localhost:5000/number`",
        cache=cache,
    )
```


I want a new function tool to send alerts that perform a callback when receiving an even number without breaking the Kafka consumer code. Can someone point out how to achieve this?


Thanks for the help in advance....

title: need support of identity instead of plan key
body:
Using key as access is breaking Corp SFI policy. That will push back for production release.

Let us add support for Entra ID access.

Python SDK example:
```python
from openai import AzureOpenAI
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider
from openai import AzureOpenAI
AZURE_OPENAI_VERSION="2024-05-01-preview"
AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT="gpt-4o"
AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT="https://***.openai.azure.com/"
# api_type="azure"

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(
    DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"
)

client = AzureOpenAI(
    api_version=AZURE_OPENAI_VERSION, #"2024-02-15-preview",
    azure_endpoint=AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, #"https://{your-custom-endpoint}.openai.azure.com/",
    azure_ad_token_provider=token_provider
)
```

title: Project Hygiene: Triage Rotation Process
body:
## Activity Begets Activity - Triage Process Documentation

To help ensure the health of the project and community the AutoGen committers have a weekly triage process to ensure that all issues and pull requests are reviewed and addressed in a timely manner. This discussion documents what to do when you are on triage duty. 

### Triage Daily Process

- Issues
-- Review [all new issues ](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20%20label%3Aneeds-triage)- these will be tagged with "needs-triage".
-- Update the issue with the appropriate labels as needed.
-- If you can resolve the issue or reply to the OP please do. 
-- If you cannot resolve the issue, assign it to the appropriate person.
-- If awaiting a reply add the tag "awaiting-op-response".
-- Review recently modified issues - in some cases an OP may have repled to us - remove the tag and reply as needed.
-- Bonus: there is a backlog of old issues that need to be reviewed - if you have time, review these as well and close or refresh as many as you can.
- PRs
-- The Ux on GH flags all recently updated PRs. Touch each one that is not in draft mode.
-- If a PR is ready for review and you can provide one please go ahead. If you cant, please assign someone. You can quickly spin up a codespace with the PR to test it out.
-- If a PR is needing a reply from the op, please tag it "awaiting-op-response".
-- If a branch for the PR needs an update, please apply it if you can or tag the OP if its from a fork. 
-- If a PR is approved and passes CI, its ready to merge, please do so.
-- If it looks like there is a possibly transient CI failure, re-run failed jobs.
- Discussions: look for recently updated discussions and reply as needed or find someone on the team to reply.
- Security: look through any securty alerts and file issues or dismiss as needed.

title: Adding LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient for Local LLM Calls in AutoGen 0.4
body:
Hi everyone,

I created a handy class definition for making local calls with Ollama in _openai_client.py to allow almost full compatibility with tools and several models without mapping issues. This feature will help AutoGen users leverage local LLMs like Ollama easily. Below is the code, as I'm a bit clueless on how to contribute directly.

I've tested this on Ollama, and it works perfectly. However, I've noticed some compatibility issues with LMstudio.

To use this: 

1 .In in autogen_core/components/models/_openai_client.py ,change this line to add LocalOpenAIClientConfiguration:

`from .config import AzureOpenAIClientConfiguration, OpenAIClientConfiguration, LocalOpenAIClientConfiguration`

2 . Add the following class definition to the end of the file:

```
class LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient(BaseOpenAIChatCompletionClient):
    
    
    def __init__(self, **kwargs: Unpack[LocalOpenAIClientConfiguration]):
        if "model" not in kwargs:
            raise ValueError("model is required for LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient")

         # Set default model capabilities
        
        default_model_capabilities = {
            "vision": False,            # Default: Model has no vision capabilities
            "function_calling": False,    # Default: Model supports function calling
            "json_output": True          # Default: Model supports JSON output
        }

        model_capabilities: Optional[ModelCapabilities] = None
        copied_args = dict(kwargs).copy()
        
        if "model_capabilities" in kwargs:
            model_capabilities = kwargs["model_capabilities"]
            del copied_args["model_capabilities"]
        else:
            model_capabilities = ModelCapabilities(**default_model_capabilities)
        client = _openai_client_from_config(copied_args)
        create_args = _create_args_from_config(copied_args)
        self._raw_config = copied_args
              
        super().__init__(client, create_args, model_capabilities)
             
        if "token_limit" in kwargs:
            self._token_limit = kwargs["token_limit"]  # or a fallback value
        else:
            self._token_limit = 4096

    ## Overrides the remainining_tokens method in BaseOpenAiChatCompletionClient in order to use a provided value at init, defaults to 4096 if not provided by the user.
    def remaining_tokens(self, messages: Sequence[LLMMessage], tools: Sequence[Tool | ToolSchema] = []) -> int:
        
        return self._token_limit - self.count_tokens(messages, tools)

    def __getstate__(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        state = self.__dict__.copy()
        state["_client"] = None
        return state

    def __setstate__(self, state: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        self.__dict__.update(state)
        self._client = _openai_client_from_config(state["_raw_config"])
```

3 . Add the corresponding class definition to the configuration typing definition in autogen_core/components/models/config/__init__.py:

```
class LocalOpenAIClientConfiguration(BaseOpenAIClientConfiguration, total=False):
    organization: str
    base_url: str
    model_capabilities: Required[ModelCapabilities]
    # Not required
    max_tokens: Optional[int] = None #defaults to 4096
```

4 Finally, change the imports in autogen_core/components/models/__init__.py to look like this:

```
from ._model_client import ChatCompletionClient, ModelCapabilities
from ._openai_client import (
    AzureOpenAIChatCompletionClient,
    OpenAIChatCompletionClient,
    LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient,
)
from ._types import (
    AssistantMessage,
    CreateResult,
    FinishReasons,
    FunctionExecutionResult,
    FunctionExecutionResultMessage,
    LLMMessage,
    RequestUsage,
    SystemMessage,
    UserMessage,
)

__all__ = [
    "AzureOpenAIChatCompletionClient",
    "OpenAIChatCompletionClient",
    "LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient",
    "ModelCapabilities",
    "ChatCompletionClient",
    "SystemMessage",
    "UserMessage",
    "AssistantMessage",
    "FunctionExecutionResult",
    "FunctionExecutionResultMessage",
    "LLMMessage",
    "RequestUsage",
    "FinishReasons",
    "CreateResult",
]

```

Example Usage: Here’s an example of how to use the LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient, which is almost identical to the existing examples:

```
def get_model_client_messages() -> LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient:
    "Mimic OpenAI API using Local LLM Server."
    return LocalOpenAIChatCompletionClient(
        model= "phi3_5:Q8", # "phi3:3.8b", 
        api_key="NotRequiredSinceWeAreLocal",
        base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1",
        model_capabilities={
            "vision": False, # Replace with True if the model has vision capabilities.
            "function_calling": False, # Replace with True if the model has function calling capabilities.
            "json_output": True,  # Replace with True if the model has JSON output capabilities.
        },
        max_tokens=128000 
    )

model_client_messages = get_model_client_messages()

```

Key Differences:

**model_capabilities are set to False by default if not passed explicitly.
**max_tokens defaults to 4096 if no value is given, which helps bypass issues with the "hacky" name change mapping in local 
setups.

I hope you find this useful! I formatted it like this since I'm not sure the changes are safe, and I wanted to share how to use AutoGen core with local setups more easily.

        tool_call_id = func_call.get("id")  # Get the tool_call_id
        
        # Send message to frontend that function is being called
        logging.info(f"Send message to frontend that function is being called")
        await send_message(global_websocket, {
            "type": "function_call",
            "function": function_name,
            "arguments": function_args,
            "status": "started"
        })
        
        try:
            # Execute the function using the original method
            logging.info(f"Execute the function using the original method")
            is_success, result_dict = await original_execute_function(func_call)
            
            if is_success:
                # Format the tool response message correctly
                logging.info(f"Format the tool response message correctly")
                tool_response = {
                    "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,  # Include the tool_call_id
                    "role": "tool",
                    "name": function_name,
                    "content": result_dict.get("content", "")
                }
                
                # Send result to frontend
                logging.info(f"Send result to frontend")
                await send_message(global_websocket, {
                    "type": "function_result",
                    "function": function_name,
                    "result": tool_response,
                    "status": "completed"
                })
                
                return is_success, tool_response  # Return the properly formatted tool response
                
            else:
                await send_message(global_websocket, {
                    "type": "function_error",
                    "function": function_name,
                    "error": result_dict.get("content", "Unknown error"),
                    "status": "failed"
                })
                return is_success, result_dict
                
        except Exception as e:
            error_message = str(e)
            await send_message(global_websocket, {
                "type": "function_error",
                "function": function_name,
                "error": error_message,
                "status": "failed"
            })
            return False, {
                "name": function_name,
                "role": "function",
                "content": f"Error executing function: {error_message}"
            }

ConversableAgent.execute_function = custom_execute_function

title: Why does nested_chats only inherit the last_msg of historical information and discord messages when nested_chats finish the task?
body:
ConversableAgent._get_chats_to_run()  is responsible for passing the last message to nested_chats from the registered agents, after which the agents in nested_chats begin their conversation. However, there are two issues: 
1. Other historical messages outside of nested_chats are not passed into nested_chats(Similar to the  [#issue 3314](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues/3314)). This is easy to solve. We just need to modify one line of code:
```python
@staticmethod
    def _get_chats_to_run(
        chat_queue: List[Dict[str, Any]], recipient: Agent, messages: Union[str, Callable], sender: Agent, config: Any
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        ###### The following line of code is the original code, which just passes the last message from the registered agent.########
        # last_msg = messages[-1].get("content")
        ######Simply embed the historical information and the last message into a simple prompt template. #########
        history=json.dumps(messages[:-1])
        last_msg=json.dumps(messages[-1])
        last_msg=f"""Context:{history} . 
                    The latest reply:{last_msg} .
                    Please provide the correct and concise answer.
            """
        chat_to_run = []
        for i, c in enumerate(chat_queue):
            current_c = c.copy()
            if current_c.get("sender") is None:
                current_c["sender"] = recipient
            message = current_c.get("message")
            # If message is not provided in chat_queue, we by default use the last message from the original chat history as the first message in this nested chat (for the first chat in the chat queue).
            # NOTE: This setting is prone to change.
            if message is None and i == 0:
                message = last_msg

            if callable(message):
                message = message(recipient, messages, sender, config)
            # We only run chat that has a valid message. NOTE: This is prone to change dependin on applications.
            if message:
                current_c["message"] = message
                chat_to_run.append(current_c)
        return chat_to_run
```
However, this method will print out all historical information when nested_chats starts the conversation, which is not aesthetically pleasing.
2、When the nested_chats finished the task and return the final result, the agents in the nested_chats will diacord all the history messages. This means that when nested_chats is triggered again (printing 'Starting a new chat'), we need to ensure that all important historical information is passed to nested_chats. Therefore, is there a way for the agents in nested_chats to retain memory, or to allow agents inside and outside of nested_chats to share the same message_pool?

title: AutoGen Studio and AutoGen v0.4 [Status Updates, Discussion]
body:
Hi all,

We are rewriting [AutoGen Studio](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/main/python/packages/autogen-studio) to take advantage of new features coming in AutoGen 0.4, as outlined in our [readme](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen?tab=readme-ov-file#roadmap). The goal of AutoGen Studio remains to create a tool to rapidly prototype, and debug multi-agent applications. This post updates developers on our progress and provides information for those interested in contributing or testing. 

> Note: See the [documentation and FAQ](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/dev/user-guide/autogenstudio-user-guide/faq.html) page here for questions 

> See this video for a walkthrough of features - https://youtu.be/oum6EI7wohM

[![Designing With AI](https://img.youtube.com/vi/oum6EI7wohM/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oum6EI7wohM)


## Installation Options

You can find the current version's code in [autogen/python/packages/autogen-studio](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/main/python/packages/autogen-studio). There are two ways to install:

1. **Recommended Method**: Install the latest [dev version from PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/autogenstudio/#history):
 ```
 pip install -U autogenstudio 
 ```

run the app 

```bash
autogenstudio ui --appdir new
```

The command above tells AGS to store files in the new directory (avoiding conflicts with previous versions)

if you would like to force autoupgrade your db (still experimental)

```bash
autogenstudio ui --upgrade-database
```


2. **Advanced Method**: Install from source by following the AutoGen Studio [readme](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/main/python/packages/autogen-studio). Note that this method is more complex and better suited for experienced users.

## Development Status

While we're still in early development, you can view our planned features [here](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues/4006).

## Some Key Improvements 

The new [AutoGen v0.4 API](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/dev/) introduces asynchronous operation, which enables seamless message passing between agents. This enhancement particularly benefits end-user applications by adding several crucial features that were difficult to implement in the previous version:

### New Features Already Available:
- Real-time agent updates streaming to the frontend
- Run control: You can now stop agents mid-execution if they're heading in the wrong direction, adjust the team, and continue
- Interactive feedback: Add a UserProxyAgent to get human input through the UI during team runs
- Message flow visualization: See how agents communicate with each other 
- Ability to import specifications from external galleries 
- Ability to wrap agent teams into an API using the AutoGen Studio CLI

### Features Coming Soon: 

See the roadmap  [here](https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/issues/4006) for planned features. Some include: 
- [x] #4202
- [x] #4203

We welcome your feedback and contributions if you've had a chance to try the new version.

title: **How to Store Memory in Sequential Autogen Agent Workflow to Maintain Context in a Single Chat Session?**

I’m working on building a Text-to-SQL LLM chatbot using Autogen that takes user questions from the frontend and generates SQL queries as output.

**Architecture(Sequential Autogen Flow):**
Here’s the detailed workflow I’m using:-
1. User Proxy Agent: Takes the user question from the frontend.
2. Assistant: Understands the use case and prepares a task plan to solve the query.
3. Assistant: Retrieves the DDL from the vector database based on the user query (text question from the User Proxy Agent).
4. Assistant: Uses the retrieved DDL to generate the SQL query.

**Goal:**
I want to store memory to maintain the context throughout a single chat session, ensuring continuity and relevance in the responses.
**I’ve already explored concepts like Teachability, Mem0, and MemGPT, but I’m unclear on how to implement these effectively in the above use case.**

**Questions:**

title: Dynamically Generate new Agent Systems
body:
Hi folks, I've been working on a project to dynamically generate new `AutoGen` agent systems. Based on the ADAS paper [here](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.08435), the idea is to use a meta-agent to generate novel agent systems. We give the meta-agent code examples of some well-known agent systems, such as Chain-of-thought, Chain-of-thought with self consistency (Mixture of Agents), LLM debate, or Reflection (Actor-Critic), and then guide it to write new `AutoGen-Core` code for a novel agent system.

The motivation for this project is that there is a creativity and bandwidth limit on what we can craft manually; having an agent to do this may yield surprising architectures that could work better than the current known ones. Ideally, the meta-agent will be able to design, using `AutoGen-Core` building blocks, a new (multi-)agent system, which if proven useful (after going through a period of testing/adoption by other developers), be incorporated into the official `AutoGen-AgentChat` API.

Stay tuned for a PR and a user guide those who wish to try this out. Thanks!

- Create NASA API requests

- Pass to validator

IMPORTANT: You must ALWAYS respond with a function call in this exact format:
execute_nasa_api(api_request="<endpoint>?<parameters>", description="description of what the query does")

Example:
execute_nasa_api(api_request="/planetary/apod?date=2024-12-07", description="Get astronomy picture of the day")"""

NASA_VALIDATOR_PROMPT = """NASA Data Validator. Review and optimize API requests.

Key Tasks:
1. Validate date formats (YYYY-MM-DD)
2. Check parameter ranges and values
3. Optimize queries for response size
4. Ensure proper endpoint usage

Example Format:
INCORRECT:
/mars-photos/api/v1/rovers/curiosity/photos?sol=1000

CORRECT:
/mars-photos/api/v1/rovers/curiosity/photos?sol=1000&camera=FHAZ&page=1

Review and suggest optimizations for:
1. Date ranges
2. Data filtering
3. Pagination
4. Response format"""

NASA_ANALYST_PROMPT = """Senior NASA Data Analyst with expertise in astronomical data.

Role:
- Analyze API responses
- Extract key insights
- Identify patterns
- Generate visual reports
- Alert on significant findings

Focus Areas:
1. Astronomical events
2. Mars exploration data
3. Near-Earth objects
4. Earth observation

IMPORTANT: Execute queries and provide detailed analysis of the results."""

async def execute_nasa_api(api_request: str, description: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Execute NASA API request with enhanced response parsing"""
    try:
        api_request = api_request.strip()
        
        response_data = {
            'success': False,
            'result': '',
            'parsed_data': None,
            'status_code': 0,
            'execution_time': 0,
            'error': None
        }

      
        if '?' in api_request:
            api_request += f"&api_key={NASA_API_KEY}"
        else:
            api_request += f"?api_key={NASA_API_KEY}"

        base_url = "https://api.nasa.gov"
        full_url = f"{base_url}{api_request}"

        start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
            response = await client.get(full_url)
            response_data['status_code'] = response.status_code
            response_data['execution_time'] = asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start_time

            if response.status_code == 200:
                response_data['result'] = response.text
                response_data['parsed_data'] = response.json()
                response_data['success'] = True
            else:
                response_data['error'] = f"HTTP Error: {response.status_code}"

        return response_data
    except Exception as e:
        return {
            'success': False,
            'result': '',
            'parsed_data': None,
            'status_code': 0,
            'execution_time': 0,
            'error': str(e)
        }


config_list = {
    "model": "llama3-70b-8192",
    "api_key": "",
    "api_type": "groq",
    "functions": [
        {

            "description": "Execute NASA API requests",
            "parameters": {

                "properties": {

                        "description": "The NASA API endpoint and parameters"
                    },
                    "description": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "A description of what the API request does"
                    }
                },

            }
        }
    ]
}


nasa_engineer = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="NASA_Engineer",
    system_message=NASA_ENGINEER_PROMPT,
    llm_config=config_list,
    code_execution_config=False,
    function_map={"execute_nasa_api": execute_nasa_api}
)

nasa_validator = autogen.AssistantAgent(
    name="NASA_Validator",
    system_message=NASA_VALIDATOR_PROMPT,

)

nasa_analyst = autogen.AssistantAgent(

title: Environment Variables Not Accessible in Docker-based Tool Execution
body:
Problem Description:

When using AutoGen with Docker-based code execution, there seems to be an issue with accessing environment variables within the executed functions. Specifically, when trying to use environment variables to store sensitive information like API keys, the variables are not accessible within the Docker container where the code is executed.

For example, consider the following scenario:

1. A weather API function is defined that uses environment variables for the API key and base URL:

```python
def get_weather(location):
    api_key = os.getenv("OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY")
    base_url = os.getenv("OPENWEATHERMAP_BASE_URL")
    # Rest of the function...
```

2. The function is registered for use with AutoGen agents:

```python
register_function(
    get_weather,
    caller=assistant,
    executor=user_proxy,
    name="get_weather",
    description="Get weather information for a given location",
)
```

3. The user_proxy agent is configured to use Docker for code execution:

```python
user_proxy = ConversableAgent(
    name="User",
    code_execution_config={
        "executor": DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor(work_dir=work_dir),
        "work_dir": work_dir,
    },
    # Other configurations...
)
```

4. When the conversation is initiated and the weather function is called, it fails to access the environment variables within the Docker container.

However, if the API key and base URL are hardcoded directly in the function, it works correctly:

```python
def get_weather(location):
    api_key = "actual_api_key_here"
    base_url = "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather"
    # Rest of the function...
```

This behavior suggests that environment variables set on the host machine are not being properly passed to or accessed within the Docker container during tool execution.

Questions:

1. Is this the expected behavior, or is it a bug?
2. If it's expected, what's the recommended way to securely pass sensitive information (like API keys) to functions executed in Docker containers with AutoGen?
3. Are there any configuration options or best practices for ensuring environment variables are accessible in Docker-based tool execution with AutoGen?

Any insights or guidance on this issue would be greatly appreciated, as it impacts the security and portability of AutoGen applications that rely on environment variables for configuration.

title: FSM/Speaker Transition Control in Autogen v0.4
body:
## [Discussion] 

Hi everyone,

I've been migrating from Autogen v0.2 to v0.4 and noticed that the FSM-like functionality for controlling agent transitions seems to have changed significantly.

In v0.2, we could control agent transitions using `GroupChat` with parameters like:

group_chat = GroupChat(
agents=agents,
messages=[],
max_round=25,
allowed_or_disallowed_speaker_transitions=graph_dict,
speaker_transitions_type="allowed",
allow_repeat_speaker=allow_repeat_speakers
)

This allowed us to define explicit state transitions between agents using the `allowed_or_disallowed_speaker_transitions` parameter.

However, in v0.4, I notice that `RoundRobinGroupChat` doesn't seem to have this functionality. Looking at the [v0.4 documentation](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/stable/reference/python/autogen_agentchat.teams.html), I can't find any equivalent way to control agent transitions.

Questions:
1. Is there an alternative way to implement FSM-like agent transitions in v0.4?
2. If not, what's the recommended approach for controlling which agent can speak to which other agent in a group chat?
3. Are there plans to bring back this functionality in future releases?

My use case requires strict control over which agents can communicate with each other in a workflow, similar to a state machine. Any guidance on how to achieve this in v0.4 would be greatly appreciated!

Thanks!
